entities.name: Query CTP synthase
observations: 541 aa protein; estimated molecular mass 61.0 kDa, theoretical pI 8.37, instability index 29.31, GRAVY -0.341, and estimated charge +4.81 at pH 7.
Strong homology support for CTP synthase: 68.4–70.6% identity over 97.6–98.3% query coverage to reviewed bacterial CTP synthases.
Pfam architecture: CTP_synth_N PF06418 at residues 3–267 and GATase PF00117 at residues 303–527; Peptidase_C26 PF07722 detected at residues 368–510.
Likely catalyzes ATP-dependent conversion of UTP to CTP using glutamine or ammonia as nitrogen source; exact substrate usage is inferred from homologs, not directly assayed for this sequence.
Likely functions in de novo pyrimidine/CTP biosynthesis; homologs are cytosolic homotetramers and are regulated by GTP activation and CTP feedback inhibition.

entities.name: Q11S24 CTP synthase
observations: Reviewed Cytophaga hutchinsonii CTP synthase homolog with 70.6% identity and 97.6% query coverage to the query.
Annotated as EC 6.3.4.2, catalyzing ATP-dependent UTP amination to CTP with glutamine or ammonia.
Annotated as a homotetramer in pyrimidine metabolism; GTP activates glutamine-dependent activity and CTP inhibits allosterically.
Reference features include an N-terminal amidoligase region, C-terminal type-1 glutamine amidotransferase domain, and catalytic nucleophile at position 384.

entities.name: De novo CTP biosynthesis
observations: The query is strongly supported as a participant in de novo pyrimidine metabolism, specifically the UTP-to-CTP step.

entities.name: UTP glutamine-dependent amination
observations: Candidate reaction: UTP + L-glutamine + ATP + H2O → CTP + L-glutamate + ADP + phosphate + 2 H(+); mapped to RHEA:26426 in homolog annotations.

entities.name: Glutamine hydrolysis
observations: Candidate glutaminase half-reaction: L-glutamine + H2O → L-glutamate + NH4(+); mapped to RHEA:15889 in homolog annotations.

entities.name: UTP ammonia-dependent amination
observations: Candidate reaction: UTP + NH4(+) + ATP → CTP + ADP + phosphate + 2 H(+); mapped to RHEA:16597 in homolog annotations.
